clue.text: Smarten up in grand accommodation

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
a room is accommodation, a place to stay

explanation.surface: Someone tidying themselves up while staying somewhere luxurious.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to make oneself neat and tidy, a synonym for smarten up.

clue.text: Small step taken by male astronaut

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pace is a single step
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: Echoes Armstrong's 'one small step for man' on the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller, the older popular word for an astronaut.

clue.text: Insect collections retained in case of trouble

indicators.note: the word for collections is held within the outer letters, as something kept inside
a case is the outside covering, so only the outer letters of trouble are used

parts.note: sets are collections of things

explanation.surface: Bug collections kept safe in case something goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of trouble' reads like 'in the event of trouble', but it means the shell of the word: T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African fly that spreads sleeping sickness, a kind of insect.

clue.text: Form attachment with 007?

definitions.meaning: to form a close connection with someone
James ... is the spy agent numbered 007

explanation.surface: Whether to grow fond of the famous fictional spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for becoming attached, and the surname of Ian Fleming's secret agent.

clue.text: Weapon a lawyer in America ships

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: An American lawyer posts a weapon somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ships' looks like a verb (sends); it is the plural noun defining a fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, like the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Has foe manipulated good spy holed up here?

indicators.note: letters that are manipulated are handled and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: good as a noun means benefit or use, as in 'what's the use?'

explanation.surface: Asks whether an enemy has been working on a good agent in hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulated' is the anagram signal for 'Has foe'; 'good' is not praise but the noun meaning benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe house is a secret dwelling where agents hide or meet, so a spy might lie low there.

clue.text: Fruit stolen: is it loaded for wide distribution?

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
's is the short form of is
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Questions whether stolen fruit will be spread widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is a cluster of small iron balls fired from a cannon that scatter over a wide area.

clue.text: Snatching grouper's tail, ray or another fish

indicators.note: the word for ray grabs and holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

indicators.note: the tail of the word grouper is its final letter

explanation.surface: One fish grabbing the tail of a grouper, perhaps a ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' seems to be the fish, after grouper; it is a beam of light. 'tail' picks R from grouper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a freshwater fish, so another fish after the grouper and ray of the surface.

clue.text: Black artist leading religious school forward

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A Black artist moving a religious school ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of bold or presumptuous, the same as shameless.

clue.text: Animal in ancient times seen aboard ark?

indicators.note: being aboard a vessel means inside it, so these letters sit within the ark's word

parts.note: an ark is a boat, like Noah's
BC marks the years before Christ, ancient times

explanation.surface: An animal sighted on Noah's Ark long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobcat is a North American wild cat, a specific animal.

clue.text: Ignorant period without Sun and Times?

parts.note: with no sun there is no light, so it is dark
ages are long periods of time

explanation.surface: Sounds like life without a certain tabloid and broadsheet newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun and The Times are British newspapers, which makes the surface read as a world without the press.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dark Ages are the early medieval centuries traditionally seen as a time of lost learning.

clue.text: Brainless creature Obama replaced absorbs energy

indicators.note: the rearranged name takes another letter into itself
the letters of the name are put back in a different place

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A jibe at a former president being swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges OBAMA into AMOBA, which then takes in E.
explanation.definitionFit: The amoeba is a single-celled organism with no nervous system, so literally without a brain.

clue.text: Corner Germanic invader

definitions.meaning: a corner is where two lines meet, as in a sharp bend
the ... were a Germanic people who settled in England, giving it its name

explanation.surface: Trapping an invader from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric meeting point of lines, and a member of the tribe that settled early England.

clue.text: Fanatic from Zimbabwe's outside often

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: a lot means often, frequently

explanation.surface: A fanatic who often comes from beyond Zimbabwe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes Z and E, the ends of Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is an extreme, uncompromising enthusiast, a synonym for fanatic.

clue.text: Snatcher — from Leatherhead?

parts.note: the Surrey town's name split in two reads leather plus head: kid is goatskin leather and napper is slang for head

explanation.surface: A thief who hails from the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey, south-west of London; split as leather (KID) plus head (NAPPER, slang) it builds the snatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: One who seizes and abducts a person is a snatcher of people, built from slang for goatskin and head.

clue.text: Relatives installing large oven

indicators.note: the relatives' word sets another letter in place inside itself

parts.note: kin are your family members
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Family members putting in a big oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is a furnace for firing pottery or bricks, a type of oven.

clue.text: Nature god banking silver for heathen

indicators.note: the god's name holds the silver as a bank holds money

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A nature deity depositing silver for a non-believer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan follows a non-mainstream or polytheistic religion, as a heathen does.

clue.text: Partly spoiled, not worth considering

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so the letters are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Something partly ruined and so not worth bothering about.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trivial or meagre, too small to merit attention.

clue.text: British quiet losing leader in wild region

indicators.note: the word for quiet drops its first letter

parts.note: hush means quiet

explanation.surface: A British silence broken in the wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush is uncultivated wild country, especially in Australia or Africa.

clue.text: Courage shown in the personal column?

definitions.meaning: strength of character, firmness of resolve
playfully the column inside a person's own body, the spine

explanation.surface: Bravery displayed in the newspaper's lonely-hearts section.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit and resolve, and the spinal column that runs through each person.

clue.text: Mania uncontrolled, student becomes beast

indicators.note: letters out of control run wild into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner, as on L-plates for student drivers

explanation.surface: A student overcome by frenzy turns into a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any creature, and beast is a synonym.

clue.text: Friend who cleans out the stables?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a pal or mate
to muck out is to clear dung from a stable, so one doing it mucks

explanation.surface: A pal who does the dirty work in the stables.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a close mate, and literally one who mucks out horses.

clue.text: Lure and net damaged by rocks

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken and reordered

parts.note: rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink served on the rocks

explanation.surface: Fishing gear and a net torn on rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to tempt or attract, a synonym of lure as a verb.

clue.text: Drunken son in mum's hosiery?

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A drunk son dressed in his mother's stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are close-fitting legwear, a typical item of women's hosiery.

clue.text: Brother killed rook and flightless birds

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: A rook and some emus were killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like another bird among the emus; it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend Remus was slain by his twin Romulus, founder of Rome.

clue.text: Range of mushrooms sent back with cap trimmed

indicators.note: something sent back goes the reverse way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ceps are a kind of edible mushroom

indicators.note: trimming cuts off the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to cap is to trump or outdo

explanation.surface: A selection of mushrooms returned with their caps cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns CEPS into SPEC; 'cap' is not the mushroom top but the verb to outdo, TRUMP, 'trimmed' to TRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range, as of colours or opinions.

clue.text: Spot second article in French

parts.note: mo is short for a moment, a second
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: Seemingly asking someone to spot a second piece in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a small dark spot on the skin.

clue.text: Good old boy allowed to see Grail?

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A good old fellow given the chance to view the Holy Grail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail is said to be the cup of the Last Supper, so it is an example of a drinking cup.

clue.text: Push away social outcast making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means going the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a leper is figuratively someone shunned by society

explanation.surface: Fending off a pariah attempting a return.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive back or ward off, a synonym of push away.

clue.text: Penny and I, with hesitation, going round town that's radioactive

indicators.note: the pieces encircle the town, so it sits inside them

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation
Luton is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London

explanation.surface: Two people and a stammer travelling round a radioactive town.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTON, a town in Bedfordshire, England, sits between P and IUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutonium is a radioactive metallic element used in nuclear reactors and weapons.
